# Form

**Figma:** No Figma component: composes .Primitives/Input Label + Help-Text, Spacing/Gap and the .Primitives/Modal/Actions pairing (694:9383)  
**Import:** `import { Form, FormActions, FormField, FormFieldset, useFormState } from "@zen/design-system";`

Collect a set of values and submit them. Form is a <form noValidate> laid out as a Stack; useFormState holds values and errors and binds every Zen field in one spread; FormField labels custom controls, FormFieldset groups choices and FormActions is the footer row.

## Use it for
- Anything that saves several values at once: sign-up, settings, create/edit, checkout.
- A custom control that needs a label, help text and an error (Slider, ColorSelector, your own picker) → FormField.
- A group of Checkbox or RadioButton rows with one legend and one error → FormFieldset (kind="radio" for radios).
- The Cancel + submit footer of a page or card form → FormActions (it stacks on phones and can stick to the bottom).

## Use something else for
- A 3–8 field create/edit flow in an overlay → ModalForm, with onSubmit={form.handleSubmit}.
- Settings that apply at once → Toggle, outside any Form.
- A single inline edit (rename a title) → HeadingField, saved on blur.
- Filtering a list → Search and Chip filters; nothing to submit.

## Figma → React
| Figma | Prop | Values / notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| — | `useFormState({ initialValues, validate, onSubmit, focusOnError })` | returns values · errors · touched · isSubmitting · isValid · isDirty · submitCount · submitError · setValue · setError · setTouched · reset · handleSubmit · fieldError |
| — | `form.field · selectField · dateField · numberField · checkboxField · toggleField · radioField(name, value) · autocompleteField · richTextField` | exactly the props each Zen field takes: <InputField label="Work email" {...form.field("email")} /> |
| — | `<Form form={form} gap invalidMessage> · <Form onSubmit>` | gap lg between groups (default); a failed submit focuses the first invalid field and announces "N fields need attention" |
| .Primitives/Input Label + Help-Text | `<FormField label helpText error required optional labelTooltip labelAction>` | passes id, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, aria-invalid and aria-required to its one child |
| — | `<FormFieldset legend kind helpText error required optional direction gap hideLegend>` | kind: group · checkbox · radio (role=radiogroup) · toggle (rows md apart, full width) |
| .Primitives/Modal/Actions (Button Dual) | `<FormActions align sticky inset>` | align end (default) · start · between; form < 480px or breakpoint mobile → full-width lg buttons, Primary on top; sticky → pinned bar, Pale top line, safe-area padding |

## Props
Generated from the TypeScript source; full JSON in `docs/api/form.json`.

### Form
A `<form noValidate>` laid out as a Stack (gap lg between groups). On submit it prevents the page reload and calls `form.handleSubmit` (from `useFormState`) or `onSubmit`. When the submit fails it moves focus to the first invalid field and announces "N fields need attention" in a polite live region. <Form form={form}> <Stack gap="md"><InputField label="Work email" {...form.field("email")} />`</Stack>` `<FormActions>`<Button level="tertiary">Cancel`</Button>`<Button level="primary" type="submit">Create account`</Button>`</FormActions> `</Form>`

Also accepts `Omit<FormHTMLAttributes<HTMLFormElement>, "onSubmit" | "children">`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form` | `FormSubmitSource` | — | The state from `useFormState()`. Form submits through `form.handleSubmit`: it validates, shows every error, moves focus to the first invalid field and announces how many need attention. Pass either `form` or `onSubmit`. |
| `onSubmit` | `(event: SubmitEvent<HTMLFormElement>) => unknown` | — | Your own submit handler, called after `preventDefault()` (e.g. react-hook-form's `handleSubmit(onValid)`). Return a promise and Form waits for it; then, if any field is invalid (aria-invalid), it focuses the first one and announces the count. |
| `gap` | `"none" \| ZenScaleInput \| "giant" \| "xgiant" \| "2xgiant"` | `"lg"` | Space between the form's direct children (Figma Spacing/Gap): the groups of a form. Default lg (24px); fields inside a group use md. |
| `invalidMessage` | `(count: number) => string` | — | Screen-reader message after a failed submit. Default: the locale's "1 field needs attention" / "3 fields need attention". |
| `noValidate` | `boolean` | `true` | Skip the browser's own validation bubbles; Zen shows errors under each field. Default true. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The groups of the form, top to bottom: Stacks or Grids of fields, FormFieldsets, and FormActions last. |

### FormField
Label, help text and error for a control that has no built-in ones (Slider, ColorSelector, a custom picker). Zen inputs (InputField, SelectField…) already have label/helpText/error: use them directly. The wrapper is marked invalid while `error` is set, so Form can focus it after a failed submit.

Also accepts `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "children">`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | — | The field label (Figma Input/Label, Body/Small/Regular). Omit it only when the control carries its own label (a Checkbox). |
| `helpText` | `ReactNode` | — | One line of guidance under the control (Help-Text, Neutral). Replaced by `error` while there is one. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` | — | The error message (Help-Text, Negative). Pass `form.fieldError(name)` so it shows at the right moment. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Adds " *" to the label and aria-required to the control. Mark the few optional fields instead when most are required. |
| `optional` | `boolean` | `false` | Figma Label `Optional`: appends "(Optional)". |
| `labelTooltip` | `boolean \| ReactNode` | — | Figma Label `Tooltip-Icon`: an info icon with this text as a tooltip. |
| `labelAction` | `ReactNode` | — | Figma Label `Action`: a right-aligned link or text button ("Reset to default"). |
| `controlId` | `string` | — | id given to the control (default: generated). The label points at it. |
| `children` (required) | `ReactElement` | — | Exactly one control. It receives `id`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-required`, so it must put them on its focusable element (Slider takes aria-labelledby; your own controls should take all five). |

### FormFieldset
A `<fieldset>` + `<legend>` for a group of Checkbox, RadioButton or Toggle rows, with one help text and one error for the whole group. `kind="radio"` makes it a radiogroup. The legend uses the field label style (Body/Small/Regular).

Also accepts `Omit<FieldsetHTMLAttributes<HTMLFieldSetElement>, "children">`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `legend` (required) | `ReactNode` | — | Names the group ("Delivery speed", "Email me about"); read before each option. Required. |
| `hideLegend` | `boolean` | `false` | Hide the legend visually (screen readers still read it) when a heading right above already names the group. |
| `kind` | `"group" \| "checkbox" \| "radio" \| "toggle"` | `"group"` | What the group holds. `radio` adds role="radiogroup" (with aria-required / aria-invalid), as the RadioButton guideline asks; `toggle` spaces rows md; `checkbox`, `radio` and `group` space them sm. Default group. |
| `direction` | `"column" \| "row"` | `"column"` | Stack the options (column, default) or lay them in a wrapping row (2–3 short options). |
| `gap` | `"none" \| ZenScaleInput \| "giant" \| "xgiant" \| "2xgiant"` | — | Space between options (Figma Spacing/Gap). Default sm, or md for toggles. |
| `helpText` | `ReactNode` | — | One line of guidance for the whole group, under the options. Replaced by `error` while there is one. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` | — | The group's error ("Choose a delivery speed"). Pass `form.fieldError(name)`. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Adds " *" to the legend (and aria-required to a radio group): at least one option must be chosen. |
| `optional` | `boolean` | `false` | Figma Label `Optional`: appends "(Optional)" to the legend. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The options: Checkbox, RadioButton (sharing one `name`) or Toggle rows. |

### FormActions
The footer row of a form. Desktop: Tertiary (cancel) then Primary (submit), on the right. When the form is narrower than 480px, or inside a ZenProvider with breakpoint mobile, the buttons stack full width at size lg with Primary on top (the mobile footer pattern). `sticky` pins the row to the bottom of the scrolling area.

Also accepts `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "children">`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `align` | `"end" \| "start" \| "between"` | `"end"` | Where the buttons sit on wide layouts: `end` (default, right), `start`, or `between` (the first child alone on the left, e.g. "Delete draft", the rest on the right). Write Tertiary (cancel) first and Primary (submit) last in every case. |
| `sticky` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep the bar pinned to the bottom of the scrolling area (Surface background, Pale top line, safe-area padding). |
| `inset` | `"none" \| ZenScaleInput \| "4xl"` | — | Sticky only: side padding of the bar, e.g. lg on a full-bleed phone screen so the buttons line up with the fields. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The buttons: Tertiary (cancel) first, Primary (`type="submit"`, named for the outcome) last. |

### Types
Object shapes the props above refer to.

```ts
type FormSubmitEvent = { preventDefault?: () => void; currentTarget?: EventTarget | null }
interface FormSubmitSource { handleSubmit: (event?: FormSubmitEvent) => Promise<{ ok: boolean; errorCount: number }>; isSubmitting?: boolean; }
type ZenScale = "3xs" | "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl"
type ZenScaleInput = ZenScale | ZenScaleLong
type ZenScaleLong = "3xsmall" | "2xsmall" | "xsmall" | "small" | "medium" | "large" | "xlarge" | "2xlarge" | "3xlarge"
```

## Keyboard
| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Enter (in a field) | Submit the form (through its type="submit" Button) |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Move between fields and actions |
| (failed submit) | Focus moves to the first invalid field |
| Space | Check a Checkbox · switch a Toggle |
| ↑ ↓ ← → | Move and select within a radio FormFieldset |

## ✅ Do
- Bind fields with the helpers ({...form.field("email")}, {...form.selectField("role")}, {...form.checkboxField("terms")}); each one matches its field's own change signature.
- Show an error when the user leaves a field with a bad value or submits, and clear it as soon as the value is fixed (useFormState does both).
- Write each error as the fix: "Enter a valid email address, like name@company.com".
- Group related fields in a Stack gap md (or a Grid columns={{ mobile: 1, desktop: 2 }}); Form spaces the groups lg.
- Write Tertiary (Cancel) first and Primary (type="submit", named for the outcome) last in FormActions: Primary lands on the right, or on top when the actions stack (harness: form/actions-order, form/submit-button).
- Give every FormFieldset a legend, and kind="radio" to a group of RadioButtons (harness: form-fieldset/needs-legend, form-fieldset/radio-kind).
- Put field errors from the server on the field with setError; show a failed request (thrown by onSubmit, in submitError) in a Negative InlineMessage with a Try again action, keeping every value.
- Show progress on the submit button while isSubmitting ("Saving…").
- On a phone, use sticky FormActions so the main action stays above the home indicator while the fields scroll.
- Mark the exception: when most fields are required, label only the optional ones (labelOptional / optional).
- Using react-hook-form? Wrap each Zen field in its `<Controller>` and map value, the field's change callback (onValueChange(value) on every Zen field — or onChange(event) on the text fields — and onCheckedChange(checked) on Checkbox and Toggle), onBlur and error={fieldState.error?.message}; <Form onSubmit={handleSubmit(onValid)}> still focuses the first invalid field and announces the count.

## ❌ Don't
- Don't disable the submit button until the form is valid; let people submit, then focus and explain the first problem.
- Don't show an error while someone is still typing a new value; wait until they leave the field or submit.
- Don't put Toggles in a Form that is saved later; use a Checkbox, and keep instant Toggles outside the Form (harness: form/toggle-outside-form).
- Don't wrap InputField, SelectField & co. in FormField; they already have label, helpText and error.
- Don't nest a Form inside a ModalForm that has onSubmit (nested forms); pass form.handleSubmit to ModalForm instead.
- Don't clear the fields after a failed submit, and don't use the placeholder as the label or for instructions.

## Accessibility
- Form is a real <form noValidate>: Enter in a field submits it through the type="submit" Button (Zen Buttons default to type="button").
- A failed submit moves focus to the first invalid field (scrolled to the middle) and announces "N fields need attention" in a polite live region; handleSubmit also focuses when passed to ModalForm or a plain `<form>`.
- Zen fields set aria-invalid and link their message with aria-describedby; FormField passes the same attributes to a custom control, which must put them on its focusable element.
- FormFieldset is a `<fieldset>` named by its `<legend>`; kind="radio" adds role=radiogroup with aria-required and aria-invalid.
- Errors are Help-Text Negative (icon + text), never colour alone.

## Content
- Errors are one sentence that names the fix: "Enter your work email", "Use 4–6 digits, like 700000".
- Submit labels name the outcome ("Create account", "Save changes", "Send invite"); progress labels end with an ellipsis ("Saving…").
- Legends are short nouns or phrases ("Delivery", "Email me about").

## Harness (`npm run usage:check`)
| Rule | Severity | Checks | Suppress with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form/actions-order` | warn | FormActions lists Tertiary (cancel) first and Primary (submit) last; it puts Primary on the right, or on top when the actions stack on a phone. | `zen-allow-actions-order: <reason>` |
| `form/submit-button` | warn | One Button in FormActions is type="submit" (Zen Buttons default to type="button"), so both the button and Enter in a field submit the form. | `zen-allow-form-submit: <reason>` |
| `form/toggle-outside-form` | warn | Toggles apply at once, so they never wait for a Form's submit: use a Checkbox for values the submit saves, and keep instant Toggles outside the Form. | `zen-allow-form-toggle: <reason>` |
| `form-fieldset/needs-legend` | error | Every FormFieldset has a legend that names the group; screen readers read it before each option. | `zen-allow-fieldset-legend: <reason>` |
| `form-fieldset/radio-kind` | warn | A FormFieldset of RadioButtons sets kind="radio", so it becomes a radiogroup that carries aria-required and aria-invalid. | `zen-allow-fieldset-kind: <reason>` |
| `interaction/no-noop-handler` | warn | Every interaction a Zen control offers works: no no-op handlers (`() => {}`, `() => undefined`), which leave a field that ignores typing and ↑/↓ or a Dismiss that stays. Chat has chat/no-locked-interaction. | `zen-allow-noop-handler: <reason>` |
